vocabulary.meaning: the period of life after someone permanently stops regular paid work
examples: She is looking forward to retirement.
Retirement can bring both freedom and major lifestyle changes.

vocabulary.meaning: regular money paid to someone after retirement, usually from a government or employment scheme
examples: He receives a workplace pension.
Pension rules differ between countries.

vocabulary.meaning: to stop working permanently, usually because of age
examples: She plans to retire at sixty-five.
Some people retire gradually by reducing their hours.
Retirement savings can take decades to build.
They increased their monthly savings.

vocabulary.meaning: the age at which people normally or officially stop working or become eligible for benefits
examples: The retirement age has increased in some countries.
Not everyone wants to stop working at the official retirement age.

vocabulary.meaning: the process of organising money to meet future needs and goals
examples: Retirement requires careful financial planning.
Good financial planning considers income, expenses, and risk.

vocabulary.meaning: time when you are free from work and responsibilities
examples: Retirement gives some people more leisure time.
He plans to spend his leisure travelling and gardening.

vocabulary.meaning: the process of changing from one life stage or condition to another
examples: The transition from full-time work to retirement can feel strange.
Planning activities can make the transition easier.

vocabulary.meaning: working fewer hours than a normal full-time job
examples: She moved to part-time work before retiring completely.
Part-time employment can provide a gradual transition.

vocabulary.meaning: a person who receives a pension, especially after retirement
examples: Discounted travel is available to some pensioners.
Many pensioners remain active in community organisations.
